title: Halcyon Drift Rising Anew
premise: Cyrus Sandoval, a xenolinguist whose mind has been rewired by an alien grammar he can no longer translate back into human thought, documents the quiet collapse of Halcyon Drift, a colony erased from fleet records after the Meridian Massacre. When the deep-space vessel Anamnesis returns with its crew aged backward by temporal drift, it carries proof of what happened—and a fleet mandate to erase the colony again before the truce expires. Cyrus and the de-aged navigator Vess Okafor must recover the massacre's buried evidence while falling in love across a gap of decades neither chose. In the end, Cyrus broadcasts the colony's dying language to the entire fleet, forcing the admiralty to choose between admitting genocide or breaking the truce; they confess, Halcyon Drift is restored to the record, and Cyrus chooses to keep his altered mind, becoming the last fluent speaker of both tongues.
about_author: Ines Eriksen is a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years on remote stations where silence was part of the job description. She writes science fiction about people who keep records no one asked them to keep.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Dying Things
chapters.summary: Cyrus Sandoval records the final transmission of a neighboring outpost, narrating in his journal how he now dreams in a language with no human equivalent. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: lonely devotion—the quiet dignity of documenting what everyone else has abandoned.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Cyrus catalogs Halcyon Drift's dwindling population and failing infrastructure for an archive he knows no one will read. His sister Ama, the colony's administrator, begs him to stop living in the past. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: stubborn purpose sharpening into quiet defiance.

chapters.title: A Ship Older Than Its Crew
chapters.summary: The Anamnesis appears at the edge of the system, transmitting fleet codes that expired forty years ago. The colonists arm old defenses, expecting raiders. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: dread curdling into disbelief as the impossible ship holds position.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: The boarding party finds the Anamnesis crew biologically in their twenties though they departed as veterans—including Vess Okafor, once sixty-two, now young and missing eleven years of memory. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: vertigo of return—home remembered but unrecognizable.

chapters.title: What the Deep Space Took
chapters.summary: Vess reconstructs her lost years from ship logs: the Anamnesis passed through a temporal fold near the site of the Meridian Massacre and recorded something the fleet has spent decades denying. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: horror dawning beneath wonder.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: A fleet relay announces that the ceasefire with the Meridian Compact expires in ninety days; any provocation reopens war. The colonists realize their existence itself is the provocation. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: responsibility crushing hope.

chapters.title: Two Grammars, One Bed
chapters.summary: Cyrus is assigned to debrief Vess; her testimony exists only in a dialect his altered mind parses natively. Their sessions stretch late, intimate, dangerous. POV: alternating Cyrus/Vess. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness between two people out of sync with time.

chapters.title: Records That Never Were
chapters.summary: Vess's physical data cores are blank—scrubbed remotely by fleet security before she landed. Every proof they had evaporates. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: betrayal; the machinery of erasure working even here.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Kindness
chapters.summary: Fleet Admiral Corvane arrives personally, offering the colonists relocation, pensions, new identities—if they surrender the Anamnesis and its crew. His generosity is flawless and terrifying. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: seduction of safety versus the cost of silence.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Cyrus realizes his alien grammar maps exactly onto the gaps in the official massacre record—the language was designed to encode what human memory systems delete. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: revelation; his affliction reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Vess at Sixty-Two
chapters.summary: Vess recovers a pre-departure message from her older self, warning that she agreed to something aboard the Anamnesis she cannot remember agreeing to. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: self-distrust; fear of who she was.

chapters.title: The Colony That Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Ama digs into colonial charters and finds Halcyon Drift's founding generation refused to ratify the fleet's secrecy accord—their invisibility was punishment, not oversight. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into legal weapon.

chapters.title: Corvane's Patient War
chapters.summary: Supplies begin arriving unrequested; colonists who accept them start receiving private offers to testify that nothing happened at Meridian. The admiral is building a counter-record. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: watching corruption work gently, without violence.

chapters.title: What I Agreed To
chapters.summary: Under Cyrus's linguistic probing, Vess recovers the memory: her older self traded the crew's years for a copy of the massacre's raw sensor archive, hidden inside the ship's navigation grammar. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: shame and resolve intertwined.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Minus Twenty-Six
chapters.summary: With the truce deadline closing, Corvane moves to seize the Anamnesis; Ama stalls him with charter law while Cyrus and Vess attempt the decryption. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: desperate triage—buying hours with everything she has.

chapters.title: The Fold Speaks
chapters.summary: Decryption succeeds partially: the archive confirms the massacre but names the Compact's own commanders as co-authors, meaning disclosure could shatter the truce from both sides. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: truth revealed as a grenade with no safe side.

chapters.title: Love Against the Deadline
chapters.summary: On the eve of broadcast, Cyrus and Vess stop working; one night of choosing each other before either may be erased, imprisoned, or aged forward again. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tenderness as defiance—love claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Cyrus transmits the massacre archive embedded in the alien grammar—untranslatable to censors, comprehensible to every mind the fold has touched—across the whole fleet network. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terrifying commitment; no way back.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Listeners
chapters.summary: Across the fleet, hundreds of fold-touched crew members begin translating the broadcast aloud; Corvane orders arrests and ignites mutiny instead. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: cascade—the truth escaping all containment.

chapters.title: Truce on the Edge of a Word
chapters.summary: With the Compact demanding answers and her own officers refusing orders, Corvane faces exposure; she attempts to destroy Halcyon Drift and is relieved of command by her own bridge crew. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: the corrupt machine turning on its architect.

chapters.title: Restored to the Record
chapters.summary: The fleet formally acknowledges the Meridian Massacre, restores Halcyon Drift's charter, and opens negotiations with the Compact under mutual confession. The dead are named. POV: Ama. Emotional beat: solemn, imperfect justice—grief given a place in the ledger.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Offered experimental treatment to restore his human dreaming, Cyrus declines; he and Vess stay on Halcyon Drift, teaching the fold-language to a new generation so no record depends on one keeper again. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: peace chosen over wholeness—an ending that is also a beginning.
